Sheffield

Competitive Salary

Overview

  • We are currently recruitment on behalf of our client for an experienced Manufacturing Process Engineer to join our clients Production Engineering team in Sheffield. This is an exciting role supporting the industrialisation, scale:up and continuous improvement of their specialist manufacturing processes.
  • The role will work across manufacturing engineering, process engineering, industrialisation, equipment introduction and continuous improvement, helping to create stable, repeatable and efficient production processes.
  • This role would suit a Manufacturing Engineer, Process Engineer, Production Engineer, Industrialisation Engineer or NPI Engineer who enjoys solving manufacturing problems, improving processes and working closely with production and engineering teams.

The Opportunity

You will be involved in the introduction and optimisation of manufacturing processes and equipment, from equipment specification and supplier engagement through to FAT, SAT, commissioning and production handover. This is a hands:on manufacturing engineering role where you will be expected to get close to the process, understand problems at source and work with production and technical teams to implement practical solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the industrialisation and scale:up of CCM manufacturing processes.
  • Develop, implement and maintain manufacturing standards, including SOPs, process parameters, routings and engineering documentation.
  • Support the introduction of new manufacturing equipment and automated systems.
  • Contribute to equipment specification, supplier engagement, FAT, SAT, commissioning and production handover.
  • Provide hands:on engineering support to production, troubleshooting manufacturing issues and improving process performance.
  • Lead and support root cause analysis (RCA) and structured problem:solving activities.
  • Identify and implement process improvements to increase yield, throughput, quality and process stability.
  • Apply Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement techniques to manufacturing processes.
  • Support activities such as Kaizen, 5S and workplace/workflow optimisation where appropriate.
  • Support PFMEA/FMEA, risk assessment and engineering change activities.
  • Contribute to manufacturing CapEx and capital equipment projects.
  • Support factory layout, material flow and production workflow improvements.
  • Maintain accurate manufacturing and engineering documentation.
  • Capture and develop process knowledge to support repeatable and scalable production.
  • Work closely with Production, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance and external equipment suppliers to deliver manufacturing improvements.

About You

We are looking for an engineer with experience in manufacturing, process engineering, production engineering or industrialisation within a technically demanding production environment.

You may currently be working as a: Manufacturing Engineer, Manufacturing Process Engineer, Process Engineer, Production Engineer, Industrialisation Engineer, NPI Engineer, or Continuous Improvement Engineer. You should have experience of some or most of the following:

  • Manufacturing or process engineering within a production environment.
  • Process optimisation and continuous improvement.
  • Manufacturing equipment and/or automated production systems.
  • Equipment introduction, commissioning or production handover.
  • FAT / SAT and working with equipment suppliers.
  • Root cause analysis and structured problem solving.
  • Lean Manufacturing / Continuous Improvement / Kaizen.
  • PFMEA / FMEA and engineering change management.
  • Manufacturing documentation, SOPs and process standards.
  • Using manufacturing data to identify and deliver process improvements.
  • Interpreting engineering drawings and technical documentation.
  • Coordinating technical or manufacturing projects.
  • Working collaborativel

Job Opportunity: Manufacturing Engineer

Location: HS Marston

Company: Collins Aerospace

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defence company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

Collins Aerospace is a leader in technologically advanced, intelligent solutions that help redefine the aerospace and defence industry. With a comprehensive portfolio and deep technical expertise, we help customers meet the demands of the global market. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defence.

As a leader in the aerospace industry, we have a new and exciting opening for a Manufacturing Engineer. Reporting to the Lead Manufacturing Engineer, the Manufacturing Engineer will be responsible for supporting build and braze Operations to ensure on time delivery and uphold quality standards. The successful candidate should be an experienced Manufacturing Engineer. You will be required to work collaboratively with all disciplines including Design, Quality, Operations and Supply Chain to implement manufacturing improvements, improve product quality and reduce costs.

What you will do:

  • Creating and maintaining standard operating procedures and manufacturing specifications.
  • Support customer/internal investigations using problem resolution tools and RCCA techniques.
  • Initiate and drive continuous improvement activities to remove waste and improve efficiency, Scrap, Rework and Repair (SRR).
  • Co-ordinating corrective actions from investigations.
  • Designing and updating jigs, fixtures and tooling including creating drawings for manufacture.
  • Raising orders for new equipment as required.
  • Ensuring the Operations function is supported to facilitate on time delivery.

What You Will Learn:

Professional Development: Gain access to company-sponsored certifications and training programs, mentorship and guidance from industry leaders, opportunities to develop your leadership skills by driving exciting high-impact projects and initiatives. Thrive in a culture of continuous learning and innovation, where curiosity is encouraged and supported.

Preferred Skills & Experience:

  • Qualified to HNC/HND minimum in a relevant Engineering discipline.
  • Worked previously as a Manufacturing Engineer within aerospace, automotive or industrial sectors. Familiar with Quality, Industrialisation and Operations processes. Working with sheet metal parts, castings, complex parts machined from billet and complex assemblies.
  • Competent user of ERP systems such as SAP and MES systems such as Solumina.
  • Be able to demonstrate technical knowledge from previous roles. A good understanding of technical drawings and GD&T is essential.
  • Experience in continuous improvement activities and root cause investigation techniques such as 8D analysis, fault tree, fishbone diagrams etc.
  • Has practical experience of operating within a production or external supply chain facility.
  • Experience in Design work would be highly desirable.
  • Project management focussing on new processes (ie: moving towards automation) would also be desirable.

Why Join Us?

At Collins Aerospace, we believe in empowering our people to make a real difference. You’ll be part of a supportive, innovative team where your contributions are valued, and your career growth is encouraged. With excellent benefits, a flexible working environment, and the opportunity to work on cutting-edge aircraft interior components, this is the perfect chance to take your machining career to the next level.

What We Offer:

People are core to what we do. As such, we are committed to providing an industry leading benefits package. We offer a highly competitive salary, annual bonus, and many other benefits to include:

  • 25 days holiday (availability to buy/sell 5 extra days) plus all bank holidays.
  • Company pension Employers contribution 5% to 10% and Employee contribution (minimum 3%).
  • Cycle to work scheme.
  • Bupa Health Care.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Apply Today!

We’re looking forward to hearing from you.

RTX adheres to the principles of equal employment. All qualified applications will be given careful consideration without regard to ethnicity, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

Located in Titchfield, Hampshire, Eaton's Aerospace business stands as a global leader in aerospace fuel systems. We pride ourselves as a premier supplier of fully integrated fuel systems for fixed and rotary-wing aircraft. The Titchfield facility boasts extensive fuel and air system test facilities, facilitating comprehensive testing across a range of conditions with various fuel types.

We are seeking a Manufacturing Engineer to work within the Manufacturing Engineering Team. Supporting all operations areas of the Titchfield site. Providing day to day support to the production areas in achieving production schedule, product quality, product cost, and employee safety goals.

What You’ll Do

We are seeking a highly skilled NPI (New Product Introduction) Mechanical Manufacturing Engineer to lead the industrialisation of new aerospace products from concept through production readiness. This role is responsible for ensuring that new designs are manufacturable, cost effective, robust, and compliant with aerospace quality standards. You will collaborate closely with design engineering, operations, supply chain, and quality to deliver smooth product launches that meet programme cost, schedule, and performance goals.

Key Responsibilities

New Product Introduction (NPI) & Industrialisation

  • Lead end to end NPI activities using gated project frameworks (e.g. MRL, PPAP, AS9145, ProLaunch).
  • Develop and execute manufacturing plans, readiness reviews, and standard operations procedures.
  • Drive Design for Manufacturability & Assembly (DFMEA/PFMEA) reviews with engineering teams.
  • Define production process flow, routings, and required tooling/fixturing.
  • Support prototype builds, engineering trials, and qualification runs.
  • Creation of additive manufactured tooling, Poka Yoke fixturing, using CAD modelling.


Manufacturing Engineering

  • Develop detailed manufacturing work instructions, standard work, and build documentation.
  • Perform tolerance analysis, process capability studies, and risk assessments (PFMEA).
  • Identify opportunities for automation, process optimisation, and cost reduction.
  • Specify and validate manufacturing equipment, gauges, and special processes.
  • Support root cause analysis and implement corrective actions using structured problem solving (8D, 5 Why, DMAIC)
  • Ensure manufacturing processes comply with aerospace standards (AS9100, NADCAP, internal specs).
  • Support qualification testing, certification activities, and production readiness reviews.


Cross Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with design engineering to influence product design early in development.
  • Coordinate with supply chain and suppliers to ensure manufacturability and process capability.
  • Partner with operations to ensure smooth handover from development to production.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering is preffered
  • Experience in aerospace or a similarly regulated mechanical manufacturing environment.
  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher.


Skills

  • Demonstrated experience and involvement with NPI projects.
  • Strong working knowledge of manufacturing processes such as:
  • Assembly & integration
  • Fuel systems
  • Special processes (heat treatment, surface finishing, part marking, etc.)
  • Experience with automation, digital manufacturing, or Industry 4.0 technologies (e.g. AutoCAD, SOLIDWORKS).
  • Strong problem solving and analytical skills.
  • Excellent communication and cross functional collaboration.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and work in fast paced environments.
  • Detail oriented with a passion for process excellence.


What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and benefits package
  • Challenging projects in dynamic collaborative team
  • We make your aspirations matter – Eaton encourages internal promotion, whenever possible
  • We make your growth matter - We invest in our employees for the long term – not just with salary and benefits, but with ongoing learning and development opportunities made available through Eaton University
  • We make your contributions matter - reliability, safety, efficiency, and sustainability are at the core of our dedication to improving people’s lives and the environment through power management technologies.
  • We make your wellbeing matter – We put your health and safety first. Wellness at Eaton is more than a program, it’s about changing the environment by offering the right tools to help empower employees to make that happen

Manufacturing Automation Engineer – Witney/Oxford

£50K–£55K + £5K Bonus + Package


You will like

Developing manufacturing automation, robotics, PLC-controlled equipment and production processes for an established, innovative manufacturer in Witney, Oxford, Oxfordshire.

You will join a successful UK manufacturer producing high-quality, safety-critical products used across industry. Operating within a modern, high-volume manufacturing environment, this is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Manufacturing Automation Engineer / Automation Engineer / Production Engineer who enjoys designing, developing and improving machinery, automated equipment and factory processes.

You can expect variety, technical challenge and the satisfaction of seeing your engineering solutions implemented on the factory floor.


You will be

Working as Manufacturing Automation Engineer, taking technical ownership of automation and production engineering projects from concept through to implementation.

This is a hands-on engineering and technical leadership position rather than a traditional people-management role. Working cross-functionally with Production, Design and Quality teams, you will provide engineering expertise and help develop increasingly efficient, automated manufacturing processes. More specifically, you will:

  • Design, manage and implement new factory production processes
  • Develop manufacturing automation, machinery, tooling and production equipment
  • Undertake PLC, industrial robot and/or CNC machine programming
  • Design and build machinery, jigs, tooling and automated solutions
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI), including factory design/layout and capital equipment procurement
  • Use CAD to develop engineering designs and manufacturing solutions
  • Optimise processes to improve quality, efficiency, output and cost
  • Introduce automated inspection and quality-control processes
  • Support SPC and Design for Manufacture (DFM) activities
  • Drive continuous improvement using Kaizen and 5S
  • Develop TPM plans and support equipment reliability
  • Ensure new machinery, installations and processes meet appropriate safety requirements
  • Train production colleagues in the effective use of new and existing equipment


You will have

As Manufacturing Automation Engineer, you will have a strong practical background within production engineering, manufacturing engineering or industrial automation.

You will ideally bring a healthy mix of:

  • Manufacturing / factory automation engineering
  • PLC systems, industrial robots and/or CNC machine programming
  • Machine, tooling, jig or production equipment design
  • CAD engineering design
  • High-volume manufacturing or complex production environments
  • Production line or manufacturing process development
  • NPI and Design for Manufacture
  • Continuous improvement, Kaizen and 5S
  • ERP systems, BOMs and production routings
  • Quality systems, process control and SPC
  • Capital equipment specification, procurement and implementation
  • Strong practical problem-solving and cross-functional communication skills

Relevant engineering qualifications are valued, although practical manufacturing automation experience and a proven track record of delivering engineering improvements will be key.


You will get

As Manufacturing Automation Engineer / Automation Engineer, you will enjoy a competitive package including:

£50,000–£55,000 salary DOE + £5,000 Bonus + Package

You will also gain the opportunity to make a genuine technical impact within an established manufacturer, developing automation and manufacturing solutions that improve quality, productivity and safety.


You can apply

To the Manufacturing Automation Engineer job opportunity in Witney/Oxford, Oxfordshire, push the button on this job posting or send your CV in confidence to anthony@macstaff.co.uk.

About us

Rivan Industries (Rivan.com) is a synthetic fuel company designed to decarbonise heavy industry. We aim to make synthetic fuel cheaper than fossil fuels and sustain life on Earth by keeping the CO2 locked underground.


We design and manufacture modular synthetic fuel plants consisting of a DAC system, an Alkaline Electrolyser, and a Sabatier Reactor, vertically integrating with off-grid DC solar and the European gas-grid. We’ve recently deployed the UK’s largest synthetic fuel plant and are planning to 1000x this scale in the next 2 years.


We’re looking for a Production Engineer as we continue to expand into our new 60,000 sq ft manufacturing and R&D facility in London, and simultaneously deploy our hardware at project sites. This is someone who understands how complex electro-mechanical systems are manufactured, from raw material, to finished systems. You’ll be responsible for designing production lines, providing DFMA input, managing day to day manufacturing operational issues, and continually improving manufacturing output.


The role:

Designing of Manufacturing Production Lines

  • Our systems are always being improved. We need a Production Engineer who can design production stations, and high level factory material flow for efficient operation.
  • We operate with high flexibility. If an existing configuration is not optimal, we need someone with agency who will flag, and provide a better alternative.


Working with R&D Teams on Design for Manufacture & Assembly

  • It’s critical that design input and feedback is provided to R&D engineers via DFMA, to ensure that designs can be manufactured, and that they are optimised for cost.
  • Collaboration throughout the product lifecycle, from R&D design, all of the way through to field deployment.
  • Value Engineering will be a core part of these assessments, to ensure that we can provide the cheapest synthetic gas in the world.


Equipment/Workstation Monitoring and OEE

  • As we ramp up production, bottlenecks and constraints will appear.
  • An important part of this role is that workstation, and equipment overall equipment effectiveness is assessed, and implemented.


The role will report directly to the Production Team Lead.


Core skills:

  • 3+ years of experience as a production engineer or similar role
  • Deep understanding of industrial manufacturing processes (welding, machining, laser cutting, assembly)
  • Ability and proven experience designing manufacturing lines
  • Excels at working throughout the product lifecycle to help steer design for manufacture and assembly
  • Proven track record of manufacturing process improvement
  • Experience with MRP/ERP systems operation and development


Specifics:

  • £50 - 70k salary depending on experience
  • Significant share options as part of the early team
  • In-person work at our HQ in Bermondsey, South London
  • Extensive relocation support, including £6000 per year extra to live close to our HQ
  • Private health insurance
  • Unlimited time-off


We encourage exceptional applicants from all backgrounds to apply for this role, even if they do not meet all the requirements listed.


If you don't see a current role that fits, we also welcome open applications via our website.

High Wycombe


Copello are working with an International defence client who are seeking a motivated and skilled Manufacturing Engineer to join their dynamic team. This role offers the opportunity to design, develop, implement, and optimise manufacturing processes for antennas, avionics, logic control units and associated technologies.

As a key member of the team, you will leverage your expertise to enhance design and manufacturing efficiency while ensuring the production of high-quality products. Collaboration will be central to the role, as you’ll partner with cross-functional teams, including design, quality and production, to align objectives and streamline operations.


Key responsibilities


Manufacturing Support

  • Provide real-time technical support to resolve production issues related to paint and test processes, including equipment failures, quality concerns, and process inefficiencies.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to minimise downtime and improve reliability.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with teams (e.g., Quality Control, Production, Maintenance) to address and resolve production challenges.
  • Identify and implement opportunities for process optimisation, cost reduction, and continuous improvement.
  • Specify, design, and integrate tools, jigs, fixtures, and other manufacturing aids to streamline paint and test operations.

New Product Development

  • Mitigate risks related to component handling, paint compatibility, and test reliability.


Test & Validation

  • Provide support for functional and environmental testing, validation, and performance verification of products.
  • Coordinate with test department and production teams to resolve any discrepancies or failure modes during testing.
  • Ensure compliance with test specifications and quality standards.


Qualifications and experience

  • Qualified in Manufacturing/Mechanical/Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline, with experience in paint and test processes.
  • Proven experience in a manufacturing or production engineering role, ideally within aerospace, electronics, or similar industries.
  • Experience working within a defence environment.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, equipment, and quality systems related to paint and test.
  • Experience in identifying and delivering productivity improvements.
  • Familiarity with lean manufacturing principles and Six Sigma methodologies would be advantageous.
  • Knowledge of quality standards such as EN9100 advantageous.

Job Description

Your work environment : We are now looking to recruit a Production Engineer Metal Finishing – LSM and Dryers in the Central Production Engineering Department (PED) of Bevcan EMA. The role could be based at our centre in Wantage (UK) or preferably at one of our European plants locations. The scope of the role is to support 12 manufacturing locations in Europe (UK, France, Spain, Italy, Slovakia, Greece, Germany and Turkey) and 5 in the Middle East and North Africa (UAE, Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Tunisia). You will also be involved in project work at new greenfield sites and newly acquired manufacturing locations.

Your Mission In Crown

Join us and participate in all the improvement activities of the Metal Finishing to improve all standards of the manufacturing processes in terms of quality, cost and efficiency.

Primary areas of activity and responsibility for the role will include the Lacquer Spray Machines (LSMs), Rim Coaters (BRCs & MRCs), Over varnish units (O/V), the associating ovens: IBOs, Pin Ovens, Washer Dryers, UV ovens with all associated materials /chemicals.

  • You provide plant operational support for quality issues and support in maintenance, repairs and troubleshooting, implementing best practices and follow-up with issues and improvement projects.
  • You realise Line operation and technical audits and propose improvements opportunities through respective projects.
  • You promote the development of SOP’s, Best Practices and Cost Reduction Programmes for regular operation and changeover conditions. You deliver classroom and hands-on the job training in Metal Finishing equipment and processes.
  • You take part in the Lean Manufacturing and Sustainability strategy of the Group towards materials’ consumption reduction and process waste removal by supporting any new materials’ trials and process-challenging activities.
  • You liaise with CROWN Technology on equipment, tooling, materials and process improvements and standardisation of specifications. You pass on the local Plant Teams new technologies and operational standards and you act as an ambassador of the Company’s operational culture towards the main manufacturing-related KPIs.

About You

The successful candidate has a sound engineering background to Higher National Diploma (HND) or Degree level in in Mechanical or Industrial Engineering. You are highly experienced in 2pc engineering and process knowledge, with a safety mind-set. You have the ability to acquire and utilise knowledge in specific areas of Metal Finishing areas, focusing on Lacquer Spray Machines (LSMs), Rim Coaters (BRCs & MRCs), Overvarnish units (O/V), the associating ovens: IBOs, Pin Ovens, Washer Dryers and UV ovens.

You can show proven ability to communicate clearly and concisely at all levels and you demonstrate high levels of problem-solving, with a logical approach and effective decision-making skills. A self-starter, you are an effective team player, with strong leadership and interpersonal skills. You are as well computer literate. You are flexible to travel at short notice and for extended periods overseas with the willingness to adapt to different cultures and circumstances.

What to Expect

The Senior Manufacturing Engineer is accountable for the end-to-end definition, delivery, and continuous evolution of advanced assembly manufacturing systems for a low-volume, high-value powertrain facility.

This role provides technical leadership and strategic direction across manufacturing engineering, ensuring product designs are translated into world-class, scalable, and digitally enabled production systems that achieve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and sustainability targets across the full product lifecycle.

Operating at a systems level, the role shapes plant architecture, automation strategy, and industrialisation roadmaps, while leading cross-functional integration from early concept through launch and into operational excellence.

What You'll Do

Manufacturing System Strategy & Architecture

  • Own and define the end-to-end manufacturing system architecture, including process design, automation strategy, plant layout, and digital integration.
  • Develop and govern long-term manufacturing strategies, ensuring scalability, flexibility, and alignment with future product and technology roadmaps.
  • Lead development of line concepts, takt strategies, capacity models, and industrialisation plans.
  • Drive design-for-manufacture and design-for-assembly (DfM/DfA) at programme level, influencing product architecture decisions.
  • Champion implementation of advanced Lean Production Systems and continuous improvement frameworks.
  • Define and lead integration of MES, digital twins, and Industry 4.0 technologies to enable traceability, analytics, and real-time control.

Technical Leadership – Tooling, Equipment & Automation

  • Provide technical authority and governance over tooling, equipment, and automation strategy.
  • Lead specification, selection, and validation of complex automated systems and precision assembly technologies.
  • Establish and manage strategic supplier partnerships, including integrators and equipment vendors.
  • Oversee design reviews, FAT/SAT readiness, and technical risk mitigation.
  • Drive innovation in automation, robotics, and smart manufacturing solutions to enhance capability and competitiveness.

Who are MYT Shutters?


MYT Shutters is an international shutter manufacturer with over 300 people across the UK, Europe, Australia and China. For over 20 years, we've focused on designing, developing and manufacturing high-quality window shutters for the trade market.


Manufacturing is at the heart of what we do. We operate our own production facilities in China and Australia, giving us direct control over how our products are developed, manufactured and continuously improved. Our range includes our own patented product innovations and manufacturing solutions, developed by a small, experienced team with a strong focus on quality, precision and practical problem-solving.


We’re bringing manufacturing to the UK.


Our ambition is to become the UK's number one trade supplier of shutters — and establishing our own UK manufacturing operation is a major part of achieving that.


This is an important next step for MYT. UK manufacturing will allow us to produce closer to our customers, increase capacity, improve lead times and give us greater control over production as the UK business grows.


We're not taking over an established factory. We're building the operation from the ground up.

That means setting up the machinery and production flow, establishing processes and quality standards, building the production team and creating an operation capable of scaling significantly as demand grows.


We're looking for a Production Manager who wants to play a central role in making that happen.



The role specifics


This is a hands-on Production Manager position with responsibility for taking our new UK manufacturing operation from setup through to day-to-day production and future scale-up.


Technical Training in China


Your role will begin with 21–28 days of intensive, hands-on training at our established manufacturing facility in China, working directly alongside the experienced production teams who manufacture MYT products every day.


This will give you first-hand knowledge of our complete manufacturing process at its source, including:

  • Machinery, tooling and production software
  • End-to-end manufacturing processes
  • Product specifications and quality standards
  • Machine setup, operation and diagnostics
  • Preventative maintenance
  • Troubleshooting and minor repairs
  • Production workflows and operating procedures


The objective is for you to return to the UK with a thorough technical understanding of MYT products, machinery and manufacturing methods, ready to implement these standards within the new UK operation. Flights, accommodation, meals, translator support and required business expenses will be provided by MYT.


Setting Up UK Production


Following your training, you will take responsibility for establishing the UK production operation and preparing it for live manufacturing. Working closely with the wider MYT team, you will be responsible for:


  • Setting up tooling, machinery and production workstations
  • Establishing an efficient production flow
  • Implementing and developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
  • Establishing quality control procedures and standards
  • Planning production and build schedules
  • Managing stock holding and rotation
  • Recruiting and training the initial production team
  • Ensuring operators are trained to use machinery safely and correctly
  • Building a production environment capable of consistently meeting required lead times and quality standards



Running & Developing the Operation


Once production is live, this will remain a hands-on management role. You'll be expected to understand what's happening on the factory floor, work alongside the production team when required and continuously look for opportunities to improve efficiency, quality and output.

You'll take ownership of preventative maintenance procedures and be the first point of escalation for machinery and tooling issues, including troubleshooting, diagnostics and minor repairs to minimise production downtime.


Quality control ultimately sits with the Production Manager. Shutter manufacturing requires tight tolerances, accuracy and consistency, and you'll be responsible for ensuring our processes, SOPs, maintenance standards and team performance continue to deliver the level of quality our customers expect.


The operation will start relatively small, but we expect production demand to increase significantly throughout 2027 and beyond. As volumes grow, you'll help develop the operation through increased capacity, additional production staff and shifts.


About you


We're looking for an experienced, practical Production Manager who is comfortable taking ownership and enjoys solving problems on the factory floor.


A woodworking/manufacturing background is important, alongside experience in:


  • CNC machinery
  • Creating and implementing SOPs
  • Manufacturing and production processes
  • Quality control and working to tight tolerances
  • Production planning and build scheduling
  • Stock management and rotation
  • Preventative maintenance and machinery troubleshooting
  • People management, including recruitment, training, HR responsibilities and policy enforcement


Experience within the window coverings or shutter industry would be an advantage, but isn't essential. We will consider candidates from other manufacturing backgrounds who have the right technical and operational experience.


This role would suit someone who wants more than simply managing an established production line. You'll have the opportunity to help shape a new manufacturing operation from its early stages and develop your responsibilities as the UK business, production capacity and team grow.

You will work across complex manufacturing environments, helping suppliers strengthen their processes, increase capacity and ensure they are prepared to meet current and future production demands.

Carbometrics is a Bristol-based chemistry company designing and synthesising highly selective binding molecules for cutting-edge sensors used in hospitals, medical devices, bioprocessing and industry. Our mission is to help people with diabetes and other conditions live longer, more comfortable lives through better real-time monitoring of analytes such as glucose.


Built on over 20 years of research from Professor Anthony Davis' group at the University of Bristol, our proprietary Biomimetic Glucose Binding Molecules (GBM) underpin a glucose sensing platform capable of delivering a market-leading Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM). The same core technology, developed through our predecessor company Ziylo, was acquired by Novo Nordisk to develop smart insulins. We've since expanded into potassium, lactate, pH, CO₂ and calcium, building toward the most comprehensive continuously monitored sensor array for medical use.


We're based at Science Creates, Bristol's leading scientific incubator, alongside a highly motivated team of scientists.


Role Overview

Carbometrics is introducing an ISO 13485 Quality Management System (QMS) to support the development and manufacture of our products. As Quality Manager, you'll establish, embed and own the QMS from the ground up, building the foundations of a quality function that scales with the company.


This hands-on, high-ownership role suits someone who enjoys building something new, is comfortable working independently and with external consultants as the sole quality specialist in a small team, and wants to shape how quality is done as we move toward regulatory submission and product launch.


What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the introduction and maintenance of our ISO 13485 QMS, including document control, record-keeping and change control
  • Define, implement and improve quality processes, procedures and forms suited to a growing start-up, working with the wider team
  • Chair management review meetings and ensure actions are completed
  • Plan and lead the internal audit programme, and lead preparation for and hosting of external, supplier, certification and notified body audits
  • Own the non-conformance, CAPA and root-cause investigation process, ensuring timely resolution and tracking trends
  • Manage supplier and vendor qualification, quality agreements and supplier quality performance
  • Act as main quality contact for suppliers, contractors, auditors and, as we grow, notified bodies or regulators
  • Support science and engineering teams with QC testing, incoming material inspection and routine data review
  • Maintain a strong safety and quality culture, including timely reporting and investigation of incidents, non-conformances and learning events
  • Report on quality performance and QMS status to leadership, recommending improvement priorities
  • Keep procedures up to date as the company, products and QMS mature
  • Build strong relationships across a small, cross-functional team as a trusted advisor on quality and compliance
  • Help build out the quality function as we grow, identifying where more resource is needed
  • Contribute ideas to improve personnel safety, environmental performance and process quality

What You'll Bring

Qualifications:

  • BSc in a relevant scientific or engineering discipline (e.g. Life Sciences, Chemistry, Biomedical or Chemical Engineering), or equivalent
  • Further qualification or equivalent experience in quality management, e.g. MSc in Quality Management or ISO 13485/9001 lead auditor training

Essential skills and experience:

  • Proven experience implementing and/or managing a QMS in a regulated environment, ideally ISO 13485, ISO 9001 or equivalent (e.g. IATF 16949, AS9100)
  • Experience owning document control, record-keeping and change control, and producing high-quality documentation (SOPs, work instructions, risk assessments, forms)
  • Experience planning and leading internal audits, and preparing for and hosting external audits or certification assessments
  • Experience managing non-conformances, root-cause investigations and CAPAs through to effective closure
  • Strong numeracy, literacy and computer skills, with close attention to detail
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint)
  • Ability to work independently as the sole quality specialist, using sound judgement and handling ambiguity as new processes are established
  • Significant practical laboratory or manufacturing experience, in academia and/or industry, including standard health and safety practices
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence quality culture across a science and engineering team

Desirable skills and experience:

  • Familiarity with ISO 13485:2016, including its application to a start-up or first-time device manufacturer
  • Experience with QC testing of samples and processes (e.g. characterising incoming reagents and standards) and reviewing the data
  • Experience with maintenance, calibration and qualification of instruments and equipment
  • Awareness of the medical device Product Development Process and standards such as ISO 14971 (risk management), IEC 62304 (software) and IEC 62366 (usability)
  • Awareness of ISO 10993 for biocompatibility
  • Experience acting as or supporting a Management Representative, or preparing a company for its first regulatory or notified body assessment

What's On Offer

  • The opportunity to build and lead the quality function as the company scales
  • A base at Science Creates, working alongside a motivated team of scientists
  • The chance to shape quality at a company developing market-leading glucose sensing technology

Additional Information

You must be authorised to live and work in the UK. This role is office-based five days a week.

Closing date for applications is 6th October 2026, unless the role is filled earlier.


Carbometrics values diversity and is an equal opportunities employer, welcoming applicants who meet the requirements of the role regardless of gender, ethnic origin, disability, age, religion or sexual orientation.

Oxford Nanopore Technologies: Our goal is to bring the widest benefits to society through enabling the analysis of anything, by anyone, anywhere.

The company has developed a new generation of nanopore-based sensing technology for faster, information rich, accessible and affordable molecular analysis.

The first application is DNA/RNA sequencing, and the technology is in development for the analysis of other types of molecules including proteins.

You will own one of our two custom manufacturing tools, end to end. Both exist today as working lab prototypes. About Medasil Surgical Ltd

Medasil Surgical Ltd is a specialist medical device manufacturer based in Leeds. We manufacture medical devices within a regulated environment, with quality and compliance central to our manufacturing operations. We are seeking a Validation Engineer to join our Technical and Engineering team.


The Role

The Validation Engineer will be responsible for the planning, execution, documentation and maintenance of validation and verification activities across the company’s manufacturing operations.

The role covers the validation and verification of manufacturing equipment, processes, tooling, test methods, software, facilities and associated systems used in the manufacture of medical devices.

The Validation Engineer will work closely with Engineering, Production, Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs and other relevant departments to ensure that equipment, processes and systems are appropriately qualified and remain in a validated state throughout their lifecycle.


Key Responsibilities

  • Plan, develop and execute validation and verification activities in accordance with approved procedures, validation plans and the company’s Quality Management System.
  • Prepare and execute (IQ), (OQ) and (PQ) protocols and reports.
  • Develop validation strategies, protocols, test methods, acceptance criteria and sampling plans.
  • Validate and qualify manufacturing equipment, tooling and associated processes.
  • Work with equipment and processes including injection moulding, extrusion, compression moulding, ovens, washing, assembly, sealing and inspection/test equipment.
  • Support the preparation and review of Process FMEAs and other risk assessments.
  • Identify Critical Process Parameters (CPPs), Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) and other characteristics requiring control or verification.
  • Provide validation input into engineering and quality change controls and determine requirements for qualification, verification or revalidation.
  • Support the introduction and qualification of new equipment, processes, tooling, software and manufacturing technologies.
  • Maintain accurate, complete and traceable validation documentation and records.
  • Support internal, customer, Notified Body and regulatory audits relating to validation and engineering activities.
  • Assist with the preparation and maintenance of the Site Validation Master Plan, validation schedules and validation status documentation.
  • Identify opportunities for improvement in validation processes, manufacturing processes and equipment performance.

 

Experience and Knowledge

Skills and Attributes

The role requires:

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • The ability to investigate technical problems and identify appropriate root causes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • The ability to write clear validation protocols, reports, risk assessments and technical documentation.
  • Good understanding of data analysis and the ability to interpret validation and process performance data.
  • The ability to work independently and as part of a cross-functional team.
  • Good time management and organisational skills.
  • The ability to manage multiple validation activities and meet agreed deadlines.
  • The ability to adapt to changing priorities and work effectively under time constraints.
  • The ability to maintain accurate and traceable validation records.
  • The ability to communicate effectively with Engineering, Production, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, suppliers and external contractors.
  • The confidence to challenge processes, assumptions and technical conclusions where appropriate and provide evidence-based recommendations.
  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel, including using Excel for validation data analysis.
  • The ability to work on the manufacturing floor and within controlled/cleanroom environments where required.


Working at Medasil

The Validation Engineer will work as part of the Technical and Engineering team and will have regular interaction with Engineering, Production, Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs.

The role involves both office-based technical and documentation work and practical activity within the manufacturing environment. The successful candidate will be expected to work independently on assigned validation projects while maintaining effective communication with relevant teams.


Application

To apply for this position, please submit your CV and a covering letter outlining your relevant experience in validation, engineering and/or regulated manufacturing.

Automation Engineer – Food Manufacturing Environment (Danish Crown)

Role Purpose

The Automation Engineer is responsible for the reliability, safety, optimisation, and continuous improvement of industrial automation and control systems within Danish Crown’s food manufacturing environment.

The role ensures stable and compliant operation of automated production and utility systems in line with food safety, quality, and health & safety requirements. The position works closely with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, and IT. IT infrastructure and enterprise systems remain owned by the IT function; this role provides operational input, coordination, and system expertise to support them.

Key Responsibilities

Automation & Production Systems

  • Develop, maintain, and optimise PLC, HMI, SCADA, and MES‑related automation systems supporting production performance (e.g. OEE, SAP PM interfaces).
  • Troubleshoot automation, electrical, and process control issues across production and utilities.
  • Ensure high availability and reliable performance of automated equipment in a regulated food environment.
  • Act as the production automation interface to IT by providing requirements, impact assessments, testing support, and coordination for system changes.

Food Safety, Quality & Compliance

  • Ensure automation solutions comply with HACCP, hygienic design principles, and Danish Crown standards.
  • Support QEHS compliance, legal obligations, and internal governance.
  • Participate in risk assessments, validation, and controlled change processes for automation changes.

Continuous Improvement & Reliability

  • Drive CI initiatives targeting efficiency, uptime, yield, and waste reduction.
  • Apply RCA, FMECA, RCM, and CBM methods to reduce recurring failures.
  • Support LEAN ways of working, site performance boards, and problem‑solving routines.

CAPEX & Project Delivery

  • Provide automation input to CAPEX projects including scope definition, functional specifications, commissioning, and handover.
  • Coordinate with IT where projects affect IT‑managed systems.
  • Manage suppliers, system integrators, and contractors within the automation scope.

Maintenance & Technical Governance

  • Support specialist automation maintenance activities and standards.
  • Develop and maintain SOPs and work instructions.
  • Act as CMMS (SAP PM) super‑user from an automation and maintenance perspective.
  • Support design reviews, upgrades, and obsolescence management.

Collaboration & Capability Building

  • Work closely with operations, maintenance, engineering, quality, and IT teams.
  • Train and coach operators and technicians in automation systems and process optimisation.

The role is responsible for ensuring that products, components, substrates, documentation, cleanliness standards, meet defined requirements before progressing through production.


Your Day-to-Day Responsibilities


Incoming Quality Control

  • Inspect incoming materials, substrates, components, consumables, and supplier documentation against defined specifications. 
  • Confirm correct part numbers, revision levels, quantities, packaging condition, and traceability requirements. 
  • Identify, quarantine, and escalate non-conforming or suspect material before release to production. 
  • Maintain accurate incoming inspection records and support supplier quality follow-up where required. 

In-Process Quality Control

  • Perform quality checks across SensArray production lines, including High Temp, Etch Temp, TC, RTD, and DISIS, to confirm products and processes meet applicable standards. 
  • Verify operators are working on current SOPs, work instructions, process controls, and quality requirements. 
  • Conduct routine quality gates, process audits, and workmanship checks during key manufacturing stages. 
  • Monitor ESD, cleanliness, documentation, and product handling standards across the production area. 
  • Support containment activity and stop escalation when quality risks are identified. 



Outgoing Quality Control 

  • Complete final inspection of finished products before shipment. 
  • Review product quality records, test data, manufacturing documentation, labelling, and traceability. 
  • Confirm products meet customer, internal, packaging, and shipping requirements before release. 
  • Approve, reject, or escalate product release decisions based on inspection outcome. 

Non-Conformance & Quality Improvement 

  • Raise and support Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) for identified defects or process failures. 
  • Assist with containment, root cause investigation, corrective action, and preventive action activity. 
  • Track recurring issues, quality trends, and defect data to support continuous improvement. 
  • Work with Production, Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams to reduce risk and improve process capability.

Essential

  • Experience using microscopes, metrology equipment, or other inspection tools. 
  • Understanding of root cause analysis and continuous improvement methodologies.

Purpose

 

As an EHS Specialist, you will be under the leadership of EHS Manager giving support for daily job and specifically in one or more EHS specializations. Promote the EHS culture across the organization.

 

 

Main Responsibilities

 

  • Conducting EHS Orientation training for new employees and contractors
  • Facilitating toolbox meetings and delivering other EHS training
  • Helping with the development of EHS procedures and tracking their implementation
  • Organizing regular site safety inspections with department/area owners; reporting findings and following up on their correction & prevention
  • Following up all audit findings; and evaluate the efficiency of their corrective & preventive actions
  • Helping to organize site EHS committee meetings and following up on all actions agreed in the committee meeting
  • Keeping good/regular liaison with authorities related to Environment, Health and Safety; reporting to EHS Manager any clue of authority concerns

  • Helping with risk assessment and providing solutions to minimize risks
  • Educate, monitor, and train personnel on safe work procedures

  • Follow procedures to monitor health and safety at designated locations
  • Conduct inspections on periodic and regular basis to detect code violations, hazards, and incorrect work practices and procedures

Maintenance Electrician


Location: Whatley
Hours: Full Time | Permanent
Salary: £55,000pa plus paid Over time


Powering Performance. Keeping Operations Running.

Are you an experienced Electrical Maintenance Engineer or Electrician looking for a challenging role within a busy industrial environment?

At Heidelberg Materials, we're looking for a skilled Maintenance Electrician to help maximise the reliability, availability, and performance of our plant and equipment. Working as part of an experienced maintenance team, you'll play a key role in ensuring our operations run safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards.

This is an excellent opportunity for a proactive individual who enjoys fault finding, problem-solving, and working with a wide range of electrical systems and technologies.


What You'll Be Doing

As a Maintenance Electrician, you will be responsible for carrying out planned and reactive maintenance activities across site, helping to minimise downtime and support continuous improvement initiatives.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Diagnosing faults and carrying out electrical repairs on plant and equipment.
  • Performing preventative and corrective maintenance to maximise operational reliability.
  • Supporting plant inspections, maintenance shutdowns, and improvement projects.
  • Assisting with the implementation and commissioning of capital projects.
  • Maintaining compliance with Health & Safety, IMS, and site procedures.
  • Liaising with supervisors and operational teams on technical and safety matters.
  • Supporting the development and management of critical spare parts strategies.
  • Recording maintenance activities using SAP PM systems.
  • Participating in occasional weekend and night working during planned and emergency maintenance activities.

Technical Expertise Required


Electrical Installation & Power Distribution

  • Working knowledge of LV and HV electrical systems.
  • Experience inspecting, testing, and maintaining switchgear, transformers, and cable systems.
  • Understanding of electrical protection systems, fault-level analysis, and earth fault protection.
  • Experience working to current electrical regulations and industry standards.

Motors, Drives & Controls

  • Installation, maintenance, and fault-finding on AC/DC motors.
  • Experience with soft starters, slip-ring motors, squirrel cage motors, and liquid starters.
  • Knowledge of variable speed drives (VSDs) and motor control systems.
  • Understanding of motor vibration analysis and bearing systems.

Instrumentation & Automation

  • Experience with process instrumentation and calibration activities.
  • Knowledge of weigh systems, load cells, level control devices, gas analysers, and PID controllers.
  • Fault finding on PLC-controlled systems and associated SCADA platforms.
  • Experience with Allen Bradley, Siemens, Modicon, or similar control systems would be advantageous.

Safety & Compliance

  • Experience working with safety-critical systems and interlocks.
  • Understanding of PUWER and electrical safety regulations.
  • Commitment to maintaining the highest safety standards in an industrial environment.

What We're Looking For

You will be a practical, self-motivated individual with strong troubleshooting skills and a commitment to safe working practices.


Essential Requirements

  • Recognised electrical qualification.
  • Strong fault-finding and diagnostic experience gained within an industrial, manufacturing, quarrying, or heavy engineering environment.
  • Computer literacy and experience using maintenance management systems.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound technical decisions.
  • Flexible approach to working hours when operational requirements demand.

Desirable

  • SAP PM experience.
  • EPIC certification for mobile plant operation.
  • NVQ Level 2 in Mobile Plant Operations.
  • Knowledge of industrial gases.
  • Practical welding and burning experience.
  • Experience within the aggregates, cement, quarrying, recycling, or heavy industrial sectors.
